question: A 19-year-old African American male with a history of bipolar I disorder presents to the psychiatrist for a follow-up visit. During the session, the patient explains that for the past 2 months he has felt significantly fatigued and constipated. He is always complaining of feeling cold and has gained several pounds although his diet has not changed. A blood sample was sent for analysis, revealing the following: TSH - 6 mIU/L (nl = 0.4-4.0 mIU/L), free T4 - 0.4 ng/dL (nl = 0.7-1.9 ng/dL), and serum T4 - 2.1 mcg/dL (nl = 4.6-12 mcg/dL). Which of the following is responsible for these abnormalities?
analysis: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are indicative of hypothyroidism, characterized by elevated TSH and low free T4 levels. Among the medications listed, lithium is well-known to cause hypothyroidism as a side effect. Lithium can interfere with thyroid function, leading to decreased production of thyroid hormones and compensatory elevation of TSH. The patient's history of bipolar I disorder suggests he may be on lithium therapy, which aligns with the observed thyroid abnormalities.
